en: The *Past Adorned Aeon Sutra of the Names of the Thousand Buddhas*, also titled *The Collection of the Great Mountains of Merit of All Buddhas*,
with the Kaiyuan Supplement appended to the Liang Dynasty Catalog,
states: "If there are good sons or good daughters who hear of these [Buddhas] of the three periods and three aeons..."

If one hears the name of the Buddha and with joy, faith, and delight, extols and praises it, takes refuge and prostrates to it, and furthermore can write it down, explain it to others, or paint it, or create an image of the Buddha, or offer incense, flowers, and music, and praise the Buddha’s merits while prostrating with a sincere heart—this is superior to using the lands of all the Buddhas in the ten directions, filling them with precious jewels and pure maṇi gems piled as high as the Brahma-heaven, and practicing such giving for hundreds of thousands of kalpas.

These sons and daughters of good family, having already made offerings to these various Buddhas, shall thereafter attend upon all Buddhas throughout their successive births until they attain Buddhahood, without end. They shall all receive the prediction of enlightenment from the Buddhas within the three periods of the three eons of the past, present, and future; wherever they are born, they shall always encounter the Triple Gem. They shall be reborn in the buddha-fields of the various Buddhas with their six sense faculties complete, never falling into the eight difficult conditions. They shall obtain the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics of the Buddhas, being fully adorned and perfected.
If one can prostrate with the five limbs touching the ground and personally declare:

"I now universally pay homage to all Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time; may the three miserable realms cease, may the land be abundant and the people peaceful, and may sentient beings with false views turn toward the Right Path and resolve to attain Bodhicitta. Taking this merit, I vow that together with all sentient beings of the six realms, we shall all be born in the Land of Amitāyus Buddha."

He established a great vow, desiring that all sentient beings be born in that land, so that their physical marks and signs, wisdom, and eloquence would be like those of Amitābha Buddha; the rewards they obtain would be majestic and sublime, and their lifespan immeasurable.
